summary: Guided demobilization of tenant optimizer stack after sustained latency and spawning 5xx errors
description: Issue summary: ClearWave Labs reported a sustained rise in 95th/99th percentile latency and intermittent 5xx errors after enabling a tenant-scoped optimizer profile that combines async-batching, kv-prefetch, and aggressive per-tenant quantization. Impact: Production traffic for several routes saw elevated tail latency (95p >= 1.4s, baseline 95p ~0.45s) and ~1.2% 5xx rate for ~45 minutes, causing degraded UX for multiple customer endpoints. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-west-2, tenant id cw-prod-17, config snapshot applied 2026-03-10T01:22:00Z. Steps to reproduce: 1) On dedicated pool, enable optimizer profile cw-agg-2 on tenant cw-prod-17. 2) Send mixed-length traffic similar to ClearWave's traffic pattern (avg seq len 380 tokens, bursts of 20 concurrent requests). 3) Observe 95/99 p latency increase and occasional serving-runtime OOM/retry 5xx. Logs / traces: - Observability link: https://console.redwood.ai/obs/trace?trace_id=trace-cw-20260310-1 - Serving error snippet: "runtime: KV prefetch miss exhaustion -> worker backpressure -> request retry -> 5xx" - Autoscaler logs show transient GPU utilization spikes followed by worker restarts. Additional context: Customer had previously used conservative optimizer profiles without issues. The new profile was rolled to production via the config-service staged rollout at 2026-03-10T01:22:00Z.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Apply optimizer profile cw-agg-2 to tenant cw-prod-17 in prod us-west-2. 2) Replay traffic from ClearWave representative capture (bucket: s3://cw-replays/2026-02-28-main). 3) Monitor token-level latency, kv cache hit ratio, per-worker queue depth, and 5xx rates. 4) Observe that within 10-30 minutes the 95/99p latency climbs and 5xx errors surface.

comments: 2026-03-10 02:05 - Support (Maya): Initial triage completed. Reached out to SRE to check GPU restarts and to ClearWave for traffic capture. Assigned to Rafael for config rollback assist.

2026-03-10 02:20 - SRE (Rafael): Observed worker churn correlated with kv-prefetch saturation and large async batch windows. GPU memory peaks followed by retries. Patching a quick circuit to reduce async batch max_window to 16 for affected tenant could stabilize.
2026-03-10 03:10 - Support (Maya): Customer agreed to a controlled demobilization sequence. ETA to start: 03:30 UTC. Customer noted this is high-impact for nightly jobs between 03:00-05:00 UTC.

2026-03-10 03:36 - Engineering (Priya Anand): Executed soft-demobilize: disabled kv-prefetch for tenant, rehydrated model pin to rw-7b-fp16, and set per-tenant max_async_batch=16. Preliminary telemetry shows 95p reduced to ~0.5s and 5xx dropped to 0.02%.
2026-03-11 09:12 - Customer (ClearWave, Alan): Thanks team — telemetry looks stable this morning. Please provide recommended long-term plan and opt-profile adjustments.
2026-03-12 15:28 - Support (Rafael): Documenting follow-up actions and scheduling postmortem. Leaving ticket open for confirmation of follow-ups.
2026-03-12 16:00 - Support (Maya): Added action item to add per-tenant optimizer snapshot-and-rollback tool to backlog (ENG-issue #4578).
investigation_notes: Hypotheses tested: 1) KV-prefetch combined with aggressive quantization and large async window leads to worker memory amplification — observed memory deltas on worker containers match hypothesis. 2) Async batching increased effective sequence concurrency causing KV cache pressure; reduced max_async_batch mitigates tail. 3) Model-specific quantization mismatch (rw-13b-quant-v2) possibly exacerbates decoding memory growth — re-pinning to rw-7b-fp16 reduced memory footprint. Diagnostic queries run: queried per-worker heap, KV hit/miss ratio, and batch size distribution. Key observables: sustained kv_prefetch queue_depth spikes, increased GC cycles in container logs, and increased retry/backoff events in serving-runtime.
resolution: Short-term remediation executed: 1) Soft-demobilize runbook applied to tenant cw-prod-17 at 2026-03-10T03:36:00Z: disable kv-prefetch, set max_async_batch=16, pin model to rw-7b-fp16, and apply conservative batching thresholds. 2) Cleared the config snapshot as a new baseline and created backup snapshot id snap-20260310-cw. 3) Monitored for 48 hours; metrics normalized. Long-term actions (accepted by ENG): - Implement per-tenant snapshot-and-rollback API to allow single-command restore of prior optimizer stack. - Add a circuit-breaker that automatically demobilizes kv-prefetch for a tenant when kv_prefetch queue_depth > threshold for 3 consecutive minutes. - Add a regression rule in Optimize that simulates bursty traffic mixes before promoting optimizer profiles to production. - Convert the soft-demobilize procedure into an automated operator action with safe order: (a) reduce async batch, (b) disable kv-prefetch, (c) re-pin to stable model variant, (d) notify customer and re-enable incrementally.
follow_up_actions: 1) ENG to file implementation PR for per-tenant rollback API (ENG-4578) with ETA 2026-04-05. 2) SRE to add automated alert for 'kv_prefetch queue_depth sustained' and a runbook reference. 3) CS to coordinate with ClearWave to schedule a non-peak window for staged re-introduction tests. 4) Product to add a preflight simulator in Redwood Optimize for mixed-length burst tests. 5) Add a KB article in Console docs summarizing safe demobilization steps.
postmortem_plan: If metrics regress after re-introduction tests, declare a focused postmortem with timelines: - T+0 investigation doc (immediate) - T+48h stabilization review - T+7d customer-impact summary and resolution acceptance. Owner: Rafael Ortiz.
public_communication: Customer-facing summary to be prepared by CS: We identified optimizer profile interactions that caused KV cache pressure and batch amplification. We applied a controlled rollback to safe parameters and are building safeguards to prevent recurrence. Draft ready; awaiting final metrics confirmation before sending to ClearWave.
